sources.news_title: Trump Rolls Out Red Carpet for Chinese President Xi Jinping
sources.text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife received a high-profile welcome from President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump when they arrived in the capital region for Thursday’s state visit.
Lines of US troops stood at attention at Joint Base Andrews, the home of the president’s aircraft fleet, as F-35 fighter jets and Air Force One formed the backdrop.
A military band performed while US officials hurriedly positioned a red carpet for the Chinese president’s imposing Air China jumbo jet.
The elaborate arrival ceremony echoed the reception Trump received during his May trip to Beijing, where troops also stood at attention beside a lavish red carpet.
The presidential limousine, known as The Beast, brought Trump and Melania to the aircraft. The couple then welcomed Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, at the foot of the plane, where the leaders exchanged remarks for several minutes.
However, strong winds, the roar of aircraft engines and the absence of media access made it impossible to establish what the two leaders said after Xi landed.
A military flyover thundered above the Air Force base to mark the Chinese president’s arrival. Trump visibly winced before breaking into a smile at the deafening noise, while Xi maintained a stern expression.
Trump and Melania’s airport welcome marked the first time in more than 11 years that a US president had personally greeted a foreign leader at an airport.
President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump greet Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, after their arrival at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday
China’s first couple landed shortly before 6:00 pm local time and are scheduled to remain in the capital until Friday afternoon
A US Air Force flyover thundered overhead as Xi stood unflinching and Trump responded with a smile
According to C-SPAN, the previous occasion was in 2015, when Barack Obama welcomed Pope Francis at Joint Base Andrews.
Trump had, ironically, criticized Obama in 2012 for giving Xi a “full honors ceremony with music and cannons” during an earlier visit. “So wrong,” the then-reality television star wrote on X.
This year’s display of pomp has unsettled some Republicans who have long criticized Xi. Among them was a prominent Trump ally who condemned the president for arranging what he called a “lavish” visit for a “dictator.”
Senator Roger Wicker of Mississippi, a Trump ally in the Senate, delivered a forceful denunciation from the Senate floor on Tuesday.
“Had the White House asked me for advice, I would have suggested the president not invite Xi Jinping to Washington for such a lavish welcome,” said Wicker, chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee.
“During every minute of dialog, our commander-in-chief should keep in mind that his guest is a brutal, unelected and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose massive military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America,” Wicker added.
Despite the airport ceremony’s spectacle, the event took place under a media blackout after Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.
Representatives from Fox, CBS and NBC were present, but they did not record the proceedings as a judge considered the banned outlets’ lawsuit against the administration.
At an emergency hearing over the media restrictions, Justice Department attorney Michael Velchik asked US District Judge Timothy Kelly not to reinstate the reporters’ access until after Xi Jinping’s visit, citing national security concerns.
Tensions loom in the upcoming trade talks between Xi and Trump, who are expected to address a slew of issues from technology to the future of Tehran.
The two presidents are expected to talk about AI, technology, trade, Taiwan and Iran
Members from seemingly all the branches of the US military partook in the welcome ceremony
Besides the two having bilateral negotiations, there will also be an array of cultural and social events over the three-day visit.
A state dinner will be hosted in the White House’s East Room on Thursday evening with CEOs and Cabinet members on the invite list.
The Trumps, Xi and Madame Peng will also visit the National Archives to view historical documents. Notably, the original Declaration of Independence and Constitution are housed there.
Amid the niceties, Xi is reportedly planning to press Trump on Taiwan and a $14 billion US military package that has been approved but not yet shipped to the island nation that China claims sovereignty over.
Trade will also be top of mind as the trade truce the two struck ends on November 10 and there has yet to be a breakthrough on a range of topics, including rare-earth minerals.

sources.news_title: Trump greets Xi on tarmac in rare gesture
Trump greets China’s Xi in rare airport welcome for state visit
sources.text:
Xi says China and US should be ‘partners rather than rivals’, kicking off three-day state visit
- Donald Trump personally greeted Chinese leader Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews, marking the first such US airport welcome for a Chinese leader in six decades.
- The rare gesture highlights Trump's respect towards Xi and aims to set a positive tone for their three-day state visit amid ongoing trade tensions.
- Despite the warm welcome, significant breakthroughs are unlikely due to deep divisions on trade, Taiwan, AI, and recent sensitive incidents involving military equipment.
AI generated
BEIJING/WASHINGTON – Chinese President Xi Jinping urged cooperation with the United States, Beijing’s state media reported, hours after being greeted in Washington on the evening of Sept 23 US time by President Donald Trump.
“Our two countries should be partners rather than rivals,” Xi said in written remarks published by state news agency Xinhua, adding that “the Chinese and US peoples have enjoyed longstanding friendly exchanges, and our interests are deeply intertwined”.
The comments came ahead of closely watched talks between Trump and Xi, who shook hands on a red carpet after the Chinese leader’s arrival in the US capital.
Thorny discussion topics are expected to include trade, technological competition – particularly in artificial intelligence – and Beijing’s diplomatic and economic support for Tehran.
Xi said that he was looking “forward to in-depth exchanges with President Trump on major issues concerning our bilateral relations and the global situation”, Xinhua reported.
The countries should “work towards each other to foster a stable relationship characterised by cooperation as the mainstay, competition within bounds, manageable differences and peaceful prospects”, Xi said.
And in a nod to Trump’s signature political slogan, he said that “the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the goal of making America great again can fully go hand in hand”.
He added that the two sides should “chart a correct path for two major powers” to get along, Xinhua reported.
“I am confident we can achieve this,” said Xi. “I believe that with the joint efforts of both sides, this visit will yield fruitful results, enhance the well-being of our two peoples and bring new hope for world peace.”
He was treated to a rare personal airport welcome by Trump on Sept 23, kicking off a pomp-filled state visit aimed at smoothing superpower tensions on everything from AI to trade to Iran.
Trump and First Lady Melania shook hands with Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan after the Chinese President descended from his plane at Joint Base Andrews, a US military airfield outside Washington.
Trump, wearing a long coat and gloves, and Xi then stood side by side on the tarmac as a military band played national anthems.
A noisy flyover by two B-1 bombers clearly jolted Trump, who grimaced at the roar of jets, while his Chinese guest stood by impassively.
Trump brushed off the fact that Xi had not given him a similar airport welcome when he visited Beijing in May.
“I thought it was a great little meeting, a great greeting, and I think they appreciate it,” Trump told reporters at the White House after welcoming Xi.
The personal airport greeting – a courtesy Trump was notably denied when he visited Beijing in May – begins three days of pageantry that will include another flyover and a state banquet at the White House on Sept 24.
Six F-22 fighter jets and six F-16s were lined up on the tarmac in an apparent display of military might as US officials literally rolled out the red carpet for the Chinese leader.
But expectations of any breakthroughs are low. Analysts say the main aim of the lavish spectacle is to maintain a fragile diplomatic and trade truce between the world’s biggest economies.
Xi was accompanied by his right-hand man Cai Qi and Foreign Minister Wang Yi, among others, according to Chinese state media.
There were no Chinese chief executives in Xi’s delegation, two sources told AFP, despite the fact that top US tech bosses including the leaders of major AI companies are set to attend the Sept 24 White House state banquet.
Xi’s visit will wrap up on the morning of Sept 25 when the two presidential couples have tea at the White House and then visit the National Archives, home to the US Declaration of Independence.
The Iran war will be on the agenda, Trump confirmed on Sept 23, despite having earlier played down reports that Beijing was supplying Tehran with intelligence as the conflict drags on.
“I’ll be talking about that and many other subjects – but it’s all coming along well, including that,” Trump said when an AFP reporter asked if he would bring up Iran.
Trade war truce extended
When the two leaders sit down for their highly anticipated talks on Sept 24, they will be confronting a host of thorny issues led by fears – boosted by warnings from tech CEOs – that artificial intelligence risks wiping out humanity.
But with China and the US racing for AI supremacy there are few expectations of any deal to regulate the rapidly advancing technology.
Preliminary talks on Sept 20 between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng included discussion of creating a communication channel for AI concerns.
There was one success on Sept 23, when after further talks, Bessent announced an extension of a truce in the simmering trade war between the world’s two biggest economies.
The “economic detente” will now extend beyond its Nov 10 deadline to Jan 10, Bessent said.
Jonathan Czin of the Brookings Institution told AFP that expectations were low for any concrete results from the meeting, but “I think there will be some extension of the gentleman’s agreement”.
Analysts said that China had meanwhile begun to look past Trump, whose second term ends in early 2029, and is in many ways playing for time and using the truce to consolidate its position.
Criticism from China hawks
Trump’s five-star welcome for Xi has drawn criticism from China hawks within his own party, especially amid reports that Beijing supplied Iran with intelligence for attacks on US troops.
“Our commander-in-chief should keep in mind that his guest is a brutal, unelected and oppressive dictator,” said Republican Senator Roger Wicker, chairman of the powerful Senate Armed Services Committee.
Trump, however, has played down the need to bring up the allegations of Chinese help for Iran, justifying it on the grounds that both Beijing and Washington spy on each other.
For Trump, Xi’s visit is also a chance to focus on pageantry instead of problems at home, where the Iran war’s effect on fuel prices has sent his approval rating plummeting to historic lows ahead of midterm elections in November.
American presidents very rarely travel to the airport to greet foreign leaders, although Trump welcomed Russian President Vladimir Putin off his plane in Alaska in 2025.
The last such welcomes at Andrews – apart from papal visits – are believed to be John F. Kennedy’s welcome for British prime minister Harold Macmillan in 1962, and Dwight D. Eisenhower’s for Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev in 1959. AFP

sources.news_title: Trump meets Xi in Washington
sources.text:
President Donald Trump is hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House Thursday for a high-profile summit aimed at maintaining stability between the world’s two largest economies despite continuing disputes over trade, technology, Taiwan and Iran.
The meeting is the second between Trump and Xi this year following talks in Beijing in May. It is Xi’s first visit to Washington in more than a decade.
Trump personally greeted Xi at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday evening, an unusual presidential welcome that underscored the importance attached to the visit. It was the first time in 11 years that a U.S. president greeted a foreign leader there, according to C-SPAN.
Major breakthroughs are not expected, but trade could produce tangible results. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the countries have agreed to extend until Jan. 10 a trade truce that had been scheduled to expire in November. The agreement has prevented a return to the trade war in which tariffs imposed by the two countries exceeded 100%.
The talks could also produce agreements involving tariffs, agricultural purchases, drug trafficking and expanded communication between the two countries’ militaries. China has been considering the purchase of 200 Boeing aircraft, although no additional order has been announced.
Artificial intelligence is another potential area for cooperation. U.S. and Chinese officials have discussed establishing safeguards or communications designed to prevent AI-related incidents from escalating into a broader confrontation.
Taiwan remains among the most difficult issues. China claims the self-governed island as its territory and is expected to press Trump to reduce or halt U.S. arms sales to Taiwan. U.S. allies in Asia are watching closely for any change in Washington’s support for Taipei.
Iran is also expected to be discussed. The Trump administration would like China, a major Iranian trading partner, to pressure Tehran, but Beijing has shown little indication it is prepared to do so.
Xi arrives at the talks with considerable economic leverage. China’s global trade remains strong, and its dominance of rare-earth mineral supplies gives Beijing influence over industries dependent on the materials.
Thursday’s events include an elaborate White House welcome and a state dinner attended by leading U.S. technology executives. The visit is scheduled to continue Friday.
Source: Reuters
